dedupe_keys.name: nempy australian electricity market dispatch model

description: Nempy is a Python model from the UNSW Collaboration on Energy and Environmental Markets for simulating dispatch in the Australian National Electricity Market. It constructs market optimization problems from bids, demand, ramp limits, interconnector losses and other constraints, including frequency-control ancillary services. Results include dispatch quantities, prices and network transfers. Spatial coverage is the configured Australian market regions, with the historical workflows representing five-minute dispatch intervals. The repository supplies documented examples and a Python interface free under BSD-3-Clause. Researchers can reuse the model to test changes in bidding, generation or market constraints and compare reconstructed dispatch with observations. A limitation is that detailed historical reconstruction needs substantial source data and careful correspondence to the rules for the period being modelled. The README warns that its full historical example fetches about 54 GB, so that workflow was not run. Existing data-aemo-nemweb-market-data-reports supplies relevant market information. This review verified metadata and documentation only.
